title: Knowledge Base + Assistant
label: ENTERPRISE RAG
oneLiner: Multi-tenant company knowledge base with a permission-aware agent. Cites every answer, refuses what you're not cleared to see, and flags when documents disagree.
outcome: Upload → hybrid retrieval → role-gated, cited answers.

detail.role: Solo build, end to end: tenant-aware schema, access model, ingestion and retrieval pipeline, agent layer, and the evaluation harness.
detail.problem: Company knowledge sits in drives and chats in five versions, and leadership needs the right document at the right moment. Generic RAG chatbots answer from whatever they can see, which means they eventually leak the wrong document to the wrong person.
how_it_works: Ingest: PDF, DOCX and Markdown are parsed, chunked, embedded, and stored as versioned documents with tenant, department and clearance metadata.
Retrieve: vector + keyword search fused with RRF, then reranked. Access is enforced in Postgres via Row-Level Security before the model sees anything.
Answer: the agent responds from permitted chunks only, with citations (file, version, date).
Deny gracefully: if a restricted document matches, the user is told one exists and can request access. No title, snippet or content is revealed. Requests are logged for document owners.

decisions.choice: Authorization lives in the data layer, not the prompt.
decisions.why: The model only receives chunks the user is cleared for. Prompt-based guardrails fail under adversarial input, and row-level policies don't.
One query runs as the user. A second privileged query returns only an existence flag. The extra latency is a deliberate price for being transparent without leaking.
decisions.rejected: Single query without existence visibility, or leaky unified query

decisions.choice: One Postgres instead of a separate vector DB.
decisions.why: Permissions, versions and vectors stay in one transactional store. This fits the target scale. It isn't a claim that it beats dedicated vector databases at massive scale.
Superseded versions are archived and excluded by default. When two different documents conflict, the answer flags the conflict and shows both dates instead of silently picking one.
tenant_id and RLS are on every table, even when running a single tenant. Retrofitting isolation later means rewriting every query.
decisions.rejected: Single-tenant schema with planned future migration

differentiators: Permission-leak red-team suite: adversarial prompts run as unauthorized users; the pass condition is zero leakage.
Access-request workflow: a denied search becomes an approval request instead of a dead end.
Executive brief mode: 'prep me for the vendor meeting' produces a cited digest across only the documents that person can access. (Phase 2)
Onboarding paths: role-based reading sequences for new hires. (Phase 3)

outcomes.metric: Citation accuracy (answer supported by cited chunk)

title: Dastak: Voice Agent for Real-Estate Lead Qualification
label: VOICE AGENT
oneLiner: A Hinglish voice agent that calls new property leads within a minute, qualifies buyers, books site visits and hands brokers a scored summary.
outcome: Lead in → call in ≤60s (design target) → qualified, booked, scored.

detail.role: Solo build, end to end: telephony and agent runtime, conversation state machine, Hinglish speech handling, booking and CRM integrations, and the simulation-based eval suite.
detail.problem: Property leads go cold in minutes, but brokers call back in hours, after the buyer has already spoken to a competitor. Generic voice bots fall apart on real Indian calls: Hinglish, interruptions, 'call me later', wrong numbers.
how_it_works: Trigger: a new lead hits a webhook (form or Sheet). A consent and calling-window check runs first.
Converse: the agent calls, confirms identity, then qualifies budget, area, BHK, timeline and buyer type. It handles objections and mirrors the caller's language mix per turn.
Act: it checks calendar slots live and books the site visit. If the buyer is hot, it hands off to a human.
Report: the broker gets a summary, a lead score with the reason, and the full transcript.

decisions.why: Each stage (STT, LLM, TTS) is swappable and measurable, and I control Hinglish handling. The price is stacked latency, which I recover with streaming and a measured per-stage budget.
A state machine owns consent, required fields and handoff. The model can't skip consent or 'forget' to collect a budget.
Auto-detect versus language hints compared on my own test set, with script normalization (Devanagari/Latin) before extraction.

decisions.choice: Tool latency is masked, not hidden.
decisions.why: A short spoken filler covers calendar lookups, and the gap is measured.
Calls only to people who enquired, inside calling hours, with opt-out honored instantly.
Logic tests run as text, STT tests on recorded audio, and a small number of full audio runs. This is how I kept a rigorous eval inside free-tier limits.
decisions.rejected: Running expensive audio pipelines for simple state logic checks

differentiators: Caller Arena: simulated hostile and awkward callers (price-haggler, silent, interrupter, NRI, wrong-number, Hindi↔English switcher) produce a repeatable scorecard.
Decision trace: per call, see each state transition and latency waterfall, so 'why did the agent say that?' has an answer.
Scored leads with reasons, so brokers know whom to call first and why.

outcomes.metric: Caller Arena pass rate over [N] scenarios

detail.status_note: The demo runs over WebRTC (browser) in place of the phone leg. Real-world pilot: none yet.
next: Confirm the name 'Dastak' (check for name clashes).
Phase 2: Inbound missed-call callback, real +91 telephony (Indian SIP provider), WhatsApp follow-up.
Phase 3: Warm transfer to human broker with live context screen-pop, per-broker config, vertical adaptation (e.g. clinic).
